get.description: Newest-first, cursor-paginated by each row's `seq` (insertion order — `created_at` is only second-precision, so it can't be a cursor). Pass `before_seq` to page older history for infinite scroll; pass `after_seq` for rows newer than a known tip (e.g. after an SSE change hint). Pass `step_index` to anchor the first page at that step so a sidebar jump can load a window that is not the live tip. The client re-fetches rather than getting log content pushed over the wire.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Only rows with `seq` greater than this (newer than tip).

parameters.name: before_seq
parameters.description: Only rows with `seq` less than this (older page).

parameters.name: step_index
parameters.description: Anchor this page at the earliest log for that step, then the following `limit` rows (still returned newest-first).

parameters.name: anchor_seq
parameters.description: Anchor this page at the row with this `seq` (e.g. a direct message from `GET /runs/{runId}/messages`), then the following `limit` rows.

parameters.name: contiguous
parameters.description: With `after_seq`, return the oldest `limit` rows after the cursor (the next page toward the present) instead of the newest ones.

200.description: Log rows, newest first, plus whether another older/newer page may exist.

has_more.description: True when another older page (`before_seq` the oldest row here) may return more rows.

has_more_newer.description: True when another newer page (`after_seq` the newest row here, `contiguous`) may return more rows. False on the live tip.

workflow-log-entry.description: One log line for a run — the wire form of a `workflow_log` row (`new-workflows-db/schemas/workflow-log.ts`).

seq.description: Insertion order within the log table. The total order of log rows and the pagination cursor — `created_at` is second-precision and ties.

source_run_id.description: The run that produced this line. Differs from `run_id` when a nested `call-workflow` child produced it (its output is filed under the root run's step). Null on lines written before this was tracked.

source_step_index.description: Step index within `source_run_id` that produced this line. Null on lines written before this was tracked.

workflow-log-channel.description: Which output channel a log line belongs to, so a renderer (CLI or web) can style/route it distinctly instead of guessing from content. `terminal`: raw stdout/stderr from a subprocess the workflow ran (vite, npm, git). `agent`: output from the coding agent (what it said, what it executed). `tool`: the workflow engine's own narration (e.g. "running step 3: copy"). `agent-input`: the prompt text sent to the agent.

workflow-log-level.description: Severity of a single log line, independent of its channel.

code.description: A short, machine-readable error code, for when HTTP status codes are not sufficient.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.
message.example: The requested resource could not be found.
